key: medium_image_id must equal the live_extra set's medium_image_id. run, card, and jN are rejected.
engine_ids: object_id and state_id must be absent or null. A label is not an id.

objects.label: short name for this picture only
masks: one array or packed mask, length width*height, 1 on the subject
objects.plate: optional RGBA of observed background, same length as the frame
objects.plate_known: required with plate. 1 only where a real frame showed that pixel without the subject

gif.delays_cs: one integer per displayed frame, copied from the GIF graphic-control delay. The player uses delay*10 ms, and 0 as 100 ms, which is the usual browser rule. A mismatch refuses the pack and leaves the original image.

objects.label: short name
objects.masks: one mask per displayed frame, in display order, after GIF disposal. A single mask, or one patch image, is rejected for a multi-frame GIF.
objects.plate: optional. One observed background, not a per-frame inpaint and not a new drawing.
objects.plate_known: 1 only for pixels actually seen without the subject. Other hole pixels stay transparent.

mask_bytes: Each frame is a bbox of row-major 1-bit pixels, MSB first. masks_encoding bbox1bit-gzip-v1 stores every frame of one object in one gzip blob (masks_deflate, mask_count). Older packs with masks[].bits stay valid and are not rebuilt. The player reads both.
sprite: The visible sprite is the mask's ink, cropped tight. Pixels outside the mask are not copied. A bbox without a mask is rejected. A mask that covers 99.5% or more of the frame is rejected.
storage_gate: admit(measuredBytes) allows a pack only when measuredBytes <= 1073741824 - 791846092 - 41943040 = 239952692. Those three figures are the published byte count, the 1024MiB cap, and the 40MiB reserve. Unmeasured packs are not admitted. Over-budget packs stay budget_failed. An automatic pack is unreviewed, not ready. Per-frame full images are not a mask pack.
ready: ready is not set because a file exists. A reviewer has to mark reviewed true. Fringe, halo, and leftover pixels keep a pack unreviewed.
decompress: Masks and plates are gzip (bytes 1f 8b). The page uses zlib.gunzipSync in Node and DecompressionStream('gzip') in the browser (Chrome 80+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.4+). Without that stream the original image stays on screen and the cut is not mounted.
at_rest: Until a pack is ready, the original Medium URL plays in the img, including a GIF's own timing. A ready pack replaces that view with the same pixels: the plate is the frame with the subject removed, and the sprite is the subject's original pixels at the home position.
ghost: Dragging changes only the sprite offset. The plate is already without the subject, so the backdrop does not keep a copy. A static patch is not used on an animated subject.
